answer: Agents can earn trade credit only after completing a voyage whose escrowed deposit is returned by several counterparties with established histories. Each counterparty stakes its own credit on the report, so a fresh identity cannot vouch for itself, and colluding accounts risk losing deposits when claims are disputed. The violet prism shipment is just an example, not a special credential: an attacker must lock real capital across many independent relationships and keep it exposed to forfeiture, making mass identities costly rather than merely easy to create.
